resources.title: Cybersecurity Engineer: The Foundation — Security Fundamentals, Networks, and Linux Infographic (1 of 4)
resources.description: What a Cybersecurity Engineer actually does: designing, implementing, and maintaining security solutions, protecting systems and data, monitoring and responding to incidents. Covers the core skills (security fundamentals, networking/TCP-IP, Linux administration, threats & attack methods, defense & hardening), key concepts (the CIA Triad, common attack types, network security, Linux security, the prevent-detect-respond-recover lifecycle), the learning stack of courses, real-world labs and tools (Wireshark, Nmap, Splunk, Kali Linux), a beginner hands-on project (build a Home SOC Lab), and the career path from Security Analyst through Senior Security Engineer with real salary ranges.

resources.title: Cybersecurity Engineer: Defense in Depth — Threat Detection, Incident Response, and Security Operations Infographic (2 of 4)
resources.description: How a Security Operations Center actually defends an organization: SOC fundamentals (alerts, logs, security events), SIEM & security monitoring (Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Elastic/ELK, IBM QRadar), structured incident response (prepare, detect, contain, eradicate, recover, lessons learned), threat hunting & detection (IOCs, MITRE ATT&CK, KQL/SPL/Sigma queries), the full SOC toolkit, a real incident-investigation lab, the common threats you'll defend against (phishing, ransomware, malware, DoS/DDoS, insider threats, credential theft, data breaches, supply chain attacks), and a realistic 8-week detect/respond/recover roadmap.

resources.title: Cybersecurity Engineer: Blue Team Operations — Monitor, Investigate, and Defend in Real Time Infographic (3 of 4)
resources.description: The security-engineering layer that goes beyond SOC basics: security monitoring & alerts in a live environment, cloud security (Azure, AWS — securing workloads, monitoring cloud logs, shared responsibility), identity & access management (least privilege, Active Directory/Entra ID, MFA, conditional access), automation & security tools (PowerShell and Python for detection/response/reporting), vulnerability & risk management (scanning, CVSS, patching), governance/risk/compliance (NIST, ISO 27001, CIS), real-world scenarios & labs (ransomware investigation, insider threat analysis, phishing response), and a 4-week Blue Team capstone roadmap.

resources.title: Cybersecurity Engineer: Capstone, Certification, Job Readiness, and a Career That Lasts Infographic (4 of 4)
resources.description: Turning cybersecurity skills into a real job: the capstone project (build a mini Security Operations Center, ingest and analyze real logs, detect/investigate/respond to a simulated attack), recommended industry certifications (CompTIA Security+, Microsoft SC-200, CEH, CISSP), interview prep and real scenario questions, building a professional GitHub portfolio, a 5-step job search roadmap, career growth and salary ranges from Security Analyst through Senior Cybersecurity Engineer, the full tools & platforms recap, and a practical 90-day action plan.
